statement: Call a contiguous subarray arr[l..r] (with 0 <= l <= r < len(arr)) a mountain subarray iff there exists an index p with l < p < r such that arr[l] < arr[l+1] < ... < arr[p] and arr[p] > arr[p+1] > ... > arr[r] (strictly increasing from l up to p and strictly decreasing from p down to r; this forces r-l+1 >= 3). The function returns a result res such that: if no mountain subarray exists then res = 0; otherwise res is the length of some mountain subarray (there are indices l, p, r with r-l+1 = res satisfying the mountain condition above) and every mountain subarray has length at most res.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, 0 <= res <= len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result res (it never panics, fails, or overflows).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: The function returns a result res with res = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000, and len(arr) <= 2.

statement: The function returns a result res with res = 3 if arr[0] < arr[1] and arr[1] > arr[2], and res = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000, and len(arr) = 3.

statement: The function returns a result res with res = len(arr).
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000, and the whole array is a mountain: len(arr) >= 3 and there exists p with 0 < p < len(arr)-1 such that arr[0] < arr[1] < ... < arr[p] and arr[p] > arr[p+1] > ... > arr[len(arr)-1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res with res = len(arr), the whole array is a mountain subarray: len(arr) >= 3 and there exists p with 0 < p < len(arr)-1 such that arr[0] < arr[1] < ... < arr[p] and arr[p] > arr[p+1] > ... > arr[len(arr)-1].
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res with res > 0, there exist indices l and r with 0 <= l <= r < len(arr) such that arr[l..r] is a mountain subarray (there is p with l < p < r, arr[l] < ... < arr[p] and arr[p] > ... > arr[r]) and r-l+1 = res.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, for every l and r with 0 <= l <= r < len(arr), if arr[l..r] is a mountain subarray then r-l+1 <= res.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, res = 0 if and only if there is no mountain subarray in arr, i.e. there do not exist indices l, p, r with 0 <= l < p < r < len(arr), arr[l] < arr[l+1] < ... < arr[p], and arr[p] > arr[p+1] > ... > arr[r].
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, either res = 0 or res >= 3.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000.

statement: The result returned on arr equals the result returned on brr.
preconditions: 1 <= len(arr) <= 10000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), 0 <= arr[i] <= 10000; let brr be the reversal of arr with brr[i] = arr[len(arr)-1-i] for 0 <= i < len(arr).
